sampling_method: Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in reading order, giving a population of 1..129. Location order is the printed position of each location's first counted cell, so a table floated to the top of a page precedes the body prose printed below it (Table 1 precedes the Section 3.2 paragraph that continues onto page 6) and a paragraph broken across a page break sits where its counted numbers are printed (Appendix G's cells are on page 18 although its heading is on page 17). Within a table the walk is row-major -- printed rows top-to-bottom, left-to-right across that row's own-result columns only, skipping baseline rows and hyperparameter columns in between -- and a cell printed in a table's caption is indexed after that table's body cells, because every caption in this paper is set below its table. Ownership here happens to be per row rather than per cell, and every table states its basis: Table 1's caption claims 'BERT-Small/Base are our implementation and use the same hyperparameters as ELECTRA-Small/Base', so those two rows are the authors' own rerun of prior work and count; Table 2's caption says 'BERT dev results are from Clark et al. (2019)', so that row is a citation baseline even though Clark is this paper's first author -- the number was produced by a different artifact -- while the separate 'BERT (ours)' row is own per Section 3.4's 'As a baseline, we trained our own BERT-Large model using the same hyperparameters and training time as ELECTRA-400K'; the RoBERTa, XLNet, ALBERT, SpanBERT, TinyBERT, MobileBERT, GPT and BERT rows of Tables 2, 3, 4 and 8 are published numbers and are baselines (spot-checked: Table 8's BERT-Base row 52.1/93.5/84.8/85.8/89.2/84.6/90.5/66.4 and its GPT row 45.4/91.3/75.7/80.0/88.5/82.1/88.1/56.0 are the GLUE test figures those two papers report, and Table 4's BERT-Base/BERT rows are BERT's published SQuAD numbers); all five columns of Table 5 are own, the BERT column included, because Section 3.2 states these experiments 'use the same model size and training data as BERT-Base' and its 82.2 is exactly Table 1's BERT-Base cell, which that caption claims as the authors' implementation. The one uncertain reading in the frame is Table 1's ELMo (71.2) and GPT (78.8) GLUE dev scores: no published source reports GLUE dev averages under this paper's 8-task median-of-10 protocol and the table computes those rows' FLOPs itself (Appendix E), so both are counted as the authors' own evaluations of released models, but the caption claims only BERT-Small/Base explicitly -- neither was drawn into this sample, and if that reading is wrong those 2 cells should be is_own_result:false instead. Roles: Train FLOPs, Infer FLOPs, Params and the Speedup multipliers are compute/architecture specification and therefore hyperparameter, not result, matching dino.json's and convnext.json's exclusion of #params and GFLOPs; Table 1's 'Train Time + Hardware' column is excluded on the same footing, as a training budget rather than a measured outcome, because its five ELECTRA-Small entries (4d, 2d, 1d, 12h, 6h) are exactly proportional to the fraction of training each row records and its caption disclaims comparability ('Training times should be taken with a grain of salt as they are for different hardware and with sometimes un-optimized code') -- the treatment dino.json gives 'two 8-GPU servers over 3 days'. The aggregate columns (Table 1's GLUE, Tables 2 and 8's Avg., Table 3's Avg.* and Score, Table 5's GLUE score) are counted rather than excluded as arithmetic over the cells beside them: they are the paper's headline reported number, and the arithmetic exclusion this file applies covers deltas, not averages. Deltas: the improvement over BERT-Small is printed three times with no absolute beside it -- the introduction's '5 points on GLUE', Table 1's caption 'scoring 5 GLUE points higher than a comparable BERT model', and Section 3.3's 'it scores 5 points higher than a comparable BERT-Small model' -- and counts once at each, per the rule that each printed instance is its own cell; every other comparative figure in the paper is a ratio or a range and is excluded ('30x more compute', 'less than 1/4 of their compute', '1/20th the parameters', '1/135th the pre-training compute', 'generators 1/4-1/2 the size of the discriminator'). Section 3.3's '(which gets 84.0 GLUE score)' for BERT-Large restates Table 2's cited BERT row and is excluded as a baseline. Figures 1, 3 and 4 print axis-tick calibration and series names only, with no per-point values, so they hold 0 cells; the abstract likewise holds 0, printing only compute ratios and a training budget and no measured value. SQuAD EM and F1 are printed as separate columns in Table 4 and are separate cells; no combined 'F1/EM' token appears anywhere in this paper. Units follow what is printed: no GLUE or SQuAD cell carries a unit glyph, so units is '%' only where Section 3.1 names the underlying metric as accuracy (SST, MRPC, QQP, MNLI, QNLI, RTE, and SQuAD EM/F1) and null for CoLA (Matthews correlation), STS (Spearman correlation) and every aggregate GLUE score, which averages accuracies and correlations together. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(1, 130), 15) drew {1, 2, 12, 13, 14, 25, 29, 70, 79, 83, 91, 99, 107, 108, 122}; each label below records its draw as frame_index.
